bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Motion to discharge Senate Committee on Foreign Relations rejected by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 53. Record Vote Number: 328. (consideration: CR S3595)
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution directs the President to terminate the use of U.S. Armed Forces for hostilities against Iran unless explicitly authorized by a congressional declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force against Iran.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to stop using U.S. military forces in hostilities against Iran unless Congress has passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force against Iran. It directs the removal of armed forces from any ongoing military operations against Iran that lack explicit congressional approval. The measure reasserts Congress's constitutional role in authorizing military action.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect defense contractors and military operations by requiring withdrawal from hostilities against Iran absent congressional authorization.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would order the President to terminate the use of U.S. Armed Forces for hostilities against Iran unless explicitly authorized by a congressional declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force against Iran.
plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what the United States does abroad. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
